newsitem.title: JAPAN: High oil price erodes Japan chemical giant profit.
newsitem.headline: High oil price erodes Japan chemical giant profit.

text.p: A recent rally in global oil prices helped trigger an 82 percent tumble in the half-year profits of Japanese chemical giant Mitsubishi Chemical Corp.

Current profit at the nation's largest chemical company plunged to 2.19 billion yen ($19.2 million) for the six months to September 30, 1996, from 12.31 billion yen ($107 million) the same period a year earlier, the company said on Thursday.
"The situation surrounding the company is very severe, amid sluggish petrochemical market conditions at home and abroad as well as higher material costs," the company said in a statement.
The world's eighth biggest chemical manufacturer sees its current profit also falling by 86 percent to three billion yen ($26.3 million) for the full business year ending next March.
It foresees nil net profit for the full year after posting net profit of 8.60 billion yen ($75.4 million) a year ago.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks. Net profit is what remains after tax.
Half-year sales, however, dropped a scant 0.5 percent from a year ago to 535.57 billion yen ($4.69 billion).

Half-year sales of the company's petrochemical products suffered a 3.9 percent year-on-year drop to 285 billion yen ($2.50 billion), but those in carbon and agricultural goods such as fertilisers posted a 4.5 percent year-on-year increase.

Meanwhile, another chemical giant Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd announced that its April-September current profit slipped 10 percent year-on-year to 7.65 billion yen ($67.1 million). For the full year, it sees profit down 13 percent at 15.00 billion yen ($131 million).
Mitsui attributed the results to lower prices of synthetic textile products and higher naphtha prices which wiped out the effects of stepped-up marketing and cost reduction.
Mitsui plans to merge with Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc on October 1, 1997, to create the nation's second biggest petrochemical company. ($1=114)
